properties.description:
The shared server — not the session, and not a harness hook — keeps the working-tree export current after every graph change, coalescing bursts through a debounce, and sets the export's prev_content_hash from the export as committed on the default branch when a git repository is present.

⭐ BUILT AND VERIFIED 2026-09-12, in two halves: epoch:the-export-chains-from-main (the lineage anchor) and epoch:the-server-keeps-the-export-current (the write-through).

HOW IT WORKS: `--export-to <FILE>` turns it on — explicit, because deriving the path from export history would let one export to a scratch path silently re-target the server's writes. `reflow2_init.py` emits the flag for all three harnesses, pointed at the docs/design/<project>.json that design_record_path names. After a write the task waits two seconds of quiet, with a ten-second ceiling so a steady stream cannot starve it, then exports once.

WHY THE SERVER OWNS IT: the session is the thing that might not come back. The Stop hook that used to carry this fires once and exists in one harness, so a consumer of reflow2 in any other client never saw it.

THE LINEAGE: a written export chains from its own path at the merge-base with the default branch — not the tip, which moves underneath a long-lived branch and would make the export claim descent from work it never contained. Every export on a branch chains from the same committed ancestor, so a squash-merge lands one hop and dec:export-once-per-pr holds by construction. Outside git the previous on-disk chaining stands, with the reason stated in `chain_note`.

IT DECLINES RATHER THAN OVERWRITE. A file that no longer matches what reflow2 last wrote — a hand edit, a half-resolved merge, conflict markers that will not parse — is left alone, and the reason surfaces in loop_status' `next` rather than in a log line, because a guarantee that has silently stopped guaranteeing is worse than none. A read-only server is refused the write-through outright.

AFFORDABILITY, MEASURED: a full export of the largest design in existence is 265 ms (2026-08-25, down from 1,168 ms), and the debounce means a burst of ten changes costs one export.
properties.name: The server writes the design export through to the working tree on every change, debounced, and chains its lineage from what is committed on main
